{{Short description|Norwegian scientist}}

'''Hans Petter Langtangen''' (3 January 1962 – 10 October 2016) was a Norwegian [[scientist]] trained in [[mechanics]] and [[scientific computing]]. Langtangen was the director of the [http://cbc.simula.no/pub/ Centre for Biomedical Computing], a Norwegian [[Center of Excellence]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/prognett-sff/Centres_at_a_glance/1224067001819|title=Centres at a glance – SFF|website=www.forskningsradet.no|access-date=2016-04-18}}</ref> hosted by [[Simula Research Laboratory]]. He was a [[professor]] of scientific computing at the [[University of Oslo]], and was [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing]]'' 2011–2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/journals/sisc/board.php|title=SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing (SISC) editorial board}}</ref>

== Career ==
Langtangen held a position as Simula [[Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.simula.no/people/hpl|title=Hans Petter Langtangen's webpage at Simula Research Laboratory}}</ref> with [https://www.simula.no/ Simula Research Laboratory], Norway. In addition to his position as Director of Simula's ''Centre for Biomedical Computing'', he held several leading roles within the field of scientific computing in his time at the lab. The scientific computing activities at Simula have been awarded the top grade, Excellent, in all international evaluations 2001-2015.<ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/csstorage/flex_attachment/8212021645.pdf
| title=Research Council of Norway Annual Report 2004 (Page 55).
| access-date=2016-02-05
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508193034/http://www.forskningsradet.no/csstorage/flex_attachment/8212021645.pdf
| archive-date=2016-05-08
| url-status=dead
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Artikkel/Evaluering_av_Simula_Research_Laboratory_AS/1253951987184
| title=Research Council of Norway 2009 evaluation of Simula
| access-date=2016-02-05
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422024152/http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Artikkel/Evaluering_av_Simula_Research_Laboratory_AS/1253951987184
| archive-date=2016-04-22
| url-status=dead
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Artikkel/Evaluering_av_grunnleggende_forskning_innenfor_informasjons_og_kommunikasjonsteknologi/1253964703321
| title=Research Council of Norway 2011 evaluation of ICT research in Norway
| access-date=2016-02-05
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420231407/http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Artikkel/Evaluering_av_grunnleggende_forskning_innenfor_informasjons_og_kommunikasjonsteknologi/1253964703321
| archive-date=2016-04-20
| url-status=dead
}}</ref>

In parallel with his work at Simula Research Laboratory, Langtangen held a professorship at the University of Oslo,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mn.uio.no/ifi/english/people/aca/hpl/index.html|title=Hans Petter Langtangen – Department of Informatics|website=www.mn.uio.no|access-date=2016-04-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701194524/http://www.mn.uio.no/ifi/english/people/aca/hpl/index.html|archive-date=2016-07-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> being on 80% leave since the establishment of Simula in 2001. He joined the Department of Mathematics in 1991, but after being promoted to full Professor in Mechanics at the Department of Mathematics in 1998, he moved to a professorship in Computer Science in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mn.uio.no/ifi/english/people/aca/hpl/index.html|title=Hans Petter Langtangen – Department of Informatics|website=www.mn.uio.no|access-date=2016-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701194524/http://www.mn.uio.no/ifi/english/people/aca/hpl/index.html|archive-date=2016-07-01|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In addition to his roles at the University of Oslo and Simula Research Laboratory, Langtangen worked at the Department of Scientific Computing at [[Uppsala University]] in an adjunct position from 1999 to 2002. Prior to that, he held full-time and part-time positions as research scientist with [[SINTEF]] Applied Mathematics department from 1991 to 1997. Langtangen worked with the company Numerical Objects from 1997 to 2003; this company commercialized the [[Diffpack]] software, mainly developed by Langtangen and Are Magnus Bruaset.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.linuxtoday.com/infrastructure/2012031500739INCY|title=Linux Today – An interview with author Hans Petter Langtangen|website=www.linuxtoday.com|access-date=2016-04-19|archive-date=2012-03-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322053941/http://www.linuxtoday.com/infrastructure/2012031500739INCY|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Langtangen’s formal education was from the Department of Mathematics, University of Oslo. He held a [[MSc]] degree from 1985 and [[PhD]] degree from 1989, both within the field of [[Mechanics]].

== Research and teaching ==
Langtangen's research was interdisciplinary and revolved around applied mathematics and scientific computing with an emphasis on continuum mechanical modeling, stochastic methods and scientific software design, with applications to biomedicine and geoscience in particular. His last research is focused on cerebrospinal fluid flow in the brain and spine as well as methods for uncertainty quantification.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simula.no/people/hpl|title=Hans.Petter.Langtangen {{!}} Simula|website=www.simula.no|access-date=2016-06-08}}</ref>

Langtangen was involved in the newly established [http://cinpla.org Centre for Integrative Neuroplasticity] ([[CINPLA]]) at the University of Oslo.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cinpla.org/about/|title=About|website=CINPLA|language=en-US|access-date=2016-04-15|date=2014-09-25}}</ref> He was also involved with developing and distributing scientific software to make research results more widely accessible and help accelerate research elsewhere.

For over three decades he was active with teaching and supervision. He was particularly involved in reforming science education through developing innovative courses and textbooks in the world-leading [http://www.mn.uio.no/english/about/collaboration/cse/ Computing in Science Education project] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160410200004/http://www.mn.uio.no/english/about/collaboration/cse/ |date=2016-04-10 }} at the University of Oslo. For this work he received the [[Olav Thon Foundation]] prize for Excellence in Teaching in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cinpla.org/2016/01/14/national-education-price-awarded-to-hans-petter-langtangen/|title=Price for excellence in education awarded to Hans Petter Langtangen|last=Tennø|first=Simen|website=CINPLA|access-date=2016-04-14|date=2016-01-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ots.olavthonstiftelser.no/en/prewious-awards/2016-2/|title=Awards 2016 – The Olav Thon Foundation|website=Olav Thon Stiftelsen|language=en-US|access-date=2016-04-15|archive-date=2016-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820125007/http://ots.olavthonstiftelser.no/en/prewious-awards/2016-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Together with colleagues in the Computing in Science Education project he also received awards from NOKUT<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.regjeringen.no/no/aktuelt/utdanningskvalitetsprisen-for-2012/id679747/|title=Utdanningskvalitetsprisen for 2012|last=Kunnskapsdepartementet|date=2012-04-25|website=Regjeringen.no|language=no|access-date=2016-05-25}}</ref> and the University of Oslo<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uniforum.uio.no/nyheter/2011/08/undervisning-for-framtidig-forsking.html|title=Undervisning for framtidig forsking – Uniforum|website=www.uniforum.uio.no|access-date=2016-05-25}}</ref> for his educational contributions.

Langtangen was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|title=Artikkel: Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|website=www.dnva.no|access-date=2016-04-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927170150/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|archive-date=2011-09-27|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the European Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurasc.org/members/members.asp?Cognome=l|title=European Academy of Sciences – List of Members|website=www.eurasc.org|access-date=2016-04-22}}</ref>

On October 10, 2016, Hans Petter Langtangen died after a long battle with cancer. <ref>{{cite tweet|user=RF_UiO|author=Realistforeningen|number=785794264802398208|date=11 October 2016|title=[1/2] I går fikk vi den triste beskjeden om at Hans Petter Langtangen har gått bort. Han var en professor vi beundret og satt pris på}}</ref>

== Authorship ==
Langtangen’s early research focused on numerical methods, in particular finite element methods and preconditioning for incompressible viscous flow and flow through porous media. During the early and mid 1990s, Langtangen pioneered and developed [[Diffpack]], a general C++ software library for the finite element solution of partial differential equations. Diffpack was one of the first object-oriented libraries of its kind.{{citation needed|date=June 2016}}

Langtangen was the author of three highly cited, best-selling textbooks on the subject of scientific computing and numerical methods: ''Computational partial differential equations''&nbsp;– ''numerical methods and Diffpack programming''; ''Python scripting for computational science''; and ''A primer on scientific programming with Python''.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.no/citations?user=otZqEncAAAAJ&hl=no|title=Hans Petter Langtangen – Google Scholar-sitater|website=scholar.google.no|access-date=2016-05-25|archive-date=2016-07-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701075920/https://scholar.google.no/citations?user=otZqEncAAAAJ&hl=no|url-status=dead}}</ref> Langtangen also promoted the use of Python for scientific computing through numerous journal papers and conference talks.<ref name="auto"/>

Langtangen was the editor of the scientific computing field in ''[[Encyclopedia of Applied and Computational Mathematics]]''.{{cn|date=January 2025}} He served on the [[editorial board]]s of many [[scientific journals]], including ''[[SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing]]'', ''[[Advances in Water Resources]]'', ''[[BIT Numerical Mathematics]]'', ''[[International Journal of Computational Science and Engineering]]'' and ''[[Journal of Computational Science]]''.{{citation needed|date=June 2016}}
